object_context: Orthogonal Type-I blow-up-classification child: audit whether vorticity-direction/geometric-depletion criteria can be inherited by the Albritton–Barker finite-I ancient class without silently strengthening the Type-I state space or compactness topology. Type-II remains outside this child.
structural_coordinates: unforced whole-space 3D incompressible Navier–Stokes with viscosity normalized to 1
parabolic scaling u_lambda(x,t)=lambda u(lambda x,lambda^2 t), omega_lambda=lambda^2 omega(lambda x,lambda^2 t), so zeta=omega/|omega| is scale-invariant where omega is nonzero
Albritton–Barker Type-I uses local scale-invariant I=sup(A+C+D+E); their Theorem 1.1 yields a nontrivial mild bounded ancient solution with finite I
Albritton–Barker local compactness supplies strong L3_loc velocity convergence and weak L3/2_loc pressure convergence, with only weak derivative control at the suitable-weak level
Giga–Miura Type-I mild solution instead assumes the pointwise self-similar L-infinity rate ||u||_infty(t)<=C0(-t)^(-1/2)

Giga–Miura continuous vorticity-direction alignment on high-vorticity sets becomes spatially constant in the blow-up limit because their L-infinity mild rescaling yields locally uniform derivative/vorticity compactness

Albritton–Barker explicitly list the L-infinity self-similar rate as a stronger Type-I quantity implying their weak finite-I notion; boundedness of one popular Type-I quantity is not generally known to imply the others
the map u -> curl(u)/|curl(u)| is nonlinear and singular at zero; strong L3_loc velocity convergence plus weak H1_loc-type control does not by itself give compactness of vorticity directions
pressure localization/far field remains a separate interface from vorticity geometry; this child does not repair NS-B1a3 global critical tightness
exact self-similar profile theorems remain equation-class specific; this child concerns time-dependent ancient limits, not stationary Leray profiles

recent Grujic arXiv:2607.08866 is a geometric-depletion near-analogue but its stated critical-point/L^{3/2,infinity} vorticity concentration and logarithmic BMO-direction hypotheses are additional state-space assumptions, not consequences of finite I established here

state-space transfer question = does AB finite-I imply the stronger local L-infinity Type-I rate used by Giga–Miura, or another theorem-matched geometric class?
rigidity question = can an inherited geometric condition force a nontrivial ancient limit into a lower-dimensional/Liouville class without unproved convergence of normalized vorticity?
solved_analogues: Giga–Miura Theorem 1.1: for whole-space type-I mild solutions with ||u||_infty<=C0(-t)^(-1/2), uniform continuity of vorticity direction on high-vorticity sets excludes blow-up

near_solved_analogues: Giga–Miura Theorem 2.10: local suitable-weak criterion still assumes a local L-infinity Type-I rate and uses a compactness theorem yielding locally uniform rescaled convergence
